_comment: English translation of nouveautes.html, by version. Hand-maintained: generate_nouveautes.py merges it into stats/nouveautes-en.json. Each version mirrors the French one from the CHANGELOG: same sections, same number of points, in the same order; a section's title can be left out when _sections translates it. A version that is missing here, or no longer has the French shape, is shown in French with a notice. Text is HTML: escape < and &.

37.4.7.intro: The first rare and very rare cards get their ceremony.

points.titre: The first rare card and the first very rare card get their ceremony
points.texte: The first rare card quivers a second time, harder, and the first very rare card rises more slowly; both get a second burst of fireworks and a sentence that tells how to recognise their tier (evening sky and silver frame, starry night and gold frame). Only once per tier.

images.alt: Filmed on a Galaxy A21s. An end-of-game card pack: night falls on the screen, the back of the card rises while spinning, a purple flash passes, then the card turns over. It is “Kran” (crane), golden, in a starry night. Two badges appear above it: “New card” and “Very rare card”. Under the card, a sentence reads: “Your first very rare card! You can tell by its starry night and its gold frame.”
images.legende: The very first very rare card gets its ceremony, and a sentence that tells how to recognise it from then on.

points.titre: Rarity is spelled out
points.texte: At the top of the collection, each tier is named (“✦ 5 very rare ★ 11 rare…”) instead of bare symbols; in the card pack, a rare or very rare card announces itself as it lands.

points.titre: The cards in the Leitner box show their landscape
points.texte: In the compartments, stacked cards only showed the sky; they now show their place, season and festival, as in the collection.

points.titre: Summer birds fly in the card window
points.texte: On the open card and in the card pack, they gently flap their wings and glide, drifting only slightly. They used to be frozen in the landscape.

points.titre: The keyboard has its own name in the keyboard picker
points.texte: On Samsung phones it appeared as “Clavier luxembourgeois Luxembourg”; it is now called “🇱🇺 Lëtzebuergesch Clavier” everywhere.

points.titre: No more light strip at the edge of the window when you tilt the card
points.texte: The landscape layers now overflow the window, and their edge no longer shows as they slide.

points.titre: Cards you win make the phone vibrate, by rarity
points.texte: A light tick for an uncommon card, three quivers then the stamp’s knock for a rare one, and for a very rare one a build-up during the prelude, a full knock at the flash and the crackle of fireworks. These vibrations existed but stayed silent on some phones, including the Galaxy A21s; they now go through the same path as the relief of the collection cards. They follow the “Vibrate on keypress” setting in the keyboard settings.

37.3.0.intro: The keyboard catches a double letter typed only once.

points.titre: A forgotten double letter is corrected
points.texte: “Kafi” gives “Kaffi”, “ales” gives “alles”, “ener” gives “ënner” rather than “Energie”. Luxembourgish doubles a lot of letters, and a hurried thumb often types only one.

37.2.0.intro: The keyboard is better at catching typos.

points.titre: Two words typed without a space are split
points.texte: For “echhunn”, the bar suggests “ech hunn”. Luxembourgish compound words (“ausbruecht”, “Schoulbus”) are not split.

points.titre: A finger that lands on the next key is recognised
points.texte: For “haud”, the bar suggests “Haus” first, because the s is next to the d, before “haut”.

points.titre: Two swapped letters count as a single mistake
points.texte: “ehc” gives “ech”, “mioen” gives “Moien”.

points.titre: A typo that looks like the start of another word is still corrected
points.texte: “gir” gives “fir”, “vul” gives “vun”.

points.titre: A few typos that came from the texts used to build the dictionary have been removed from it
points.texte: “hunnn”, “dobai”, “tescht”… They were accepted as they were, and “hunnn” was even suggested under “hunn”.

images.alt: The keyboard in a messaging conversation. “echhunn” is typed without a space: the bar suggests “Ech hunn”, which is tapped. Then “geschter” without its accent: the bar suggests “gëschter”. Then “an der” with no mistake, then “schiul”, the finger having landed on the i next to the o: the bar suggests “Schoul”. Finally “gescahfft”, with two swapped letters: the bar suggests “geschafft”. The final sentence is “Ech hunn gëschter an der Schoul geschafft”. A blue dot shows each tap.
images.legende: Words run together, a missing accent, the key next door, swapped letters: you type fast, the bar suggests the right word, one tap is enough.

37.1.3.intro: Cards stay on screen when you rotate the phone.

points.titre: A card opened in the collection no longer closes
points.texte: When the phone rotates, and neither does an open compartment of the Leitner box.

points.titre: In review, the card you have just turned over stays turned over

points.texte: While a card is on screen, tilting the phone moves the card instead of rotating the screen.

points.titre: On phones, the app is now always shown upright
points.texte: Held sideways, the phone left too little room: in review, the card shrank to an icon. Tablets keep both orientations.

37.1.2.intro: The end-of-game card pack holds firm when you rotate the phone.

points.titre: Rotating the phone no longer makes the card pack disappear
points.texte: The screen keeps its orientation while the pack is open, and rotates again as soon as you close it. So you can tilt the phone to play with the card without losing it.

points.titre: In landscape, the cards you won finally appear
points.texte: The back turns over, the card shows up with its rarity effects and follows the tilt of the phone.

points.titre: The card pack’s title no longer slips under the clock and icons
points.texte: Nor does “Skip” slip under the navigation bar.

37.1.1.intro: The collection and the Leitner box respond without stuttering.

points.titre: Changing the sort order or switching to the Shelf no longer freezes the collection
points.texte: The cards already on screen are reused instead of being redrawn.

points.titre: The collection opens faster
points.texte: And its grid can be scrolled as soon as it appears.

points.titre: The first card you open turns over as quickly as the next ones
points.texte: In one smooth movement.

points.titre: Opening a compartment of the Leitner box no longer blocks the screen
points.texte: The fan of cards opens as soon as its cards are ready.

37.1.0.intro: Each rare card now has its own way of arriving.

points.titre: An uncommon card ◆◆
points.texte: Lands with a gleam of light sweeping across it.

points.titre: A rare card ★★★
points.texte: Can be sensed before it appears: the back quivers three times in the pack, the phone vibrates, then, once the card is turned over, its hallmark is stamped with a ripple.

points.titre: A very rare card ✦✦✦✦
points.texte: Changes the whole scene: night falls, the card rises as it spins, a first purple flash, then it is slowly revealed under rays of light.
Vibrations follow the phone’s settings, and everything stays understated when the phone asks for fewer animations.

37.0.1.intro: Smoother cards in the Leitner box and at the end of a game.

points.titre: The cards of the Leitner box get their landscape back
points.texte: When you opened a compartment, the cards spread out showed nothing but sky.

points.titre: Review turns its cards over without stuttering
points.texte: The card gets ready while you read the question, instead of freezing the screen in the middle of the gesture.

points.titre: So does the end-of-game card pack
points.texte: Each card you win turns over in one smooth movement.
